title: Token regen thundering herd - investigation notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad to capture commands tried, concrete observations, and running hypotheses for the recent auth -> quota spike where many clients simultaneously hit 401 then 429. Personal notes to hand off to infra/SDK owners.

High-level summary / symptom:
- Multiple customers and internal integration tests observed short bursts of errors around minute boundaries. Pattern: a few 401s appear, followed by a flood of 429s for the same API key.
- Burst duration ~= 15-35s. QPS from offending key jumps 20x from baseline.
- Error headers often include Retry-After values of 60 or 120. Some responses include X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0.
- Appears correlated with token refresh events in client SDK version v1.4.2 (reported by two customers).

Raw example responses (sanitized):
- 401 Unauthorized (when hitting /v1/generate):
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Content-Type: application/json
  Date: Wed, 18 Sep 2024 14:02:00 GMT
  Retry-After: 0
  {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key revoked or expired"}

- Followed ~5s later by many 429s:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Content-Type: application/json
  Date: Wed, 18 Sep 2024 14:02:07 GMT
  Retry-After: 60
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  {"error":"rate_limited","message":"Per-key rate limit exceeded"}

Commands used to reproduce / probe:
1) Simple curl auth test (sanitized token):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
   - Observed 401 for a small subset of tokens reproduced from SDK logs.

2) Local bulk replay using vegeta to simulate many clients after forced token rotation:
   echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate","body":"{\"input\":\"bulk test\"}","header":{"Authorization":["Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>"]}}' > target.json
   cat target.json | vegeta attack -rate=500 -duration=20s | tee results.bin | vegeta report
   - With token TTL forced to expire at t=0, observed spike of 429s starting ~2-4s after first 401.

3) SDK repro (node):
   - Run SDK v1.4.2 integration test that calls client.refreshToken() on schedule.
   - Combined with no-jitter rollout, many instances refresh within the same second -> 401s then retries at once.

Observations from logs / traces:
- Trace-level logs show large number of auth-service requests at the same timestamp for the same API key.
- Token issuance service has a short path that returns the same new token to many clients if a refresh happens close in time -> some clients reuse old token for one call (401), then immediately retry which floods the inference endpoint.
- Edge LB does not smooth by origin; traffic from many ephemeral client IPs hits the same backend pool so per-key counters get exhausted quickly.
- A few keys show cyclic behavior every 60s which matches client-side token TTL (60s) reported in SDK config.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Thundering-herd caused by synchronized token refreshes in SDK v1.4.2: clients schedule refresh at fixed TTL boundaries without jitter. A small number of 401s cause aggressive immediate retries, which exceed per-key quotas.
2) Token rotation semantics: when token rotates, there is a short window where some servers still accept old token while others don't -> inconsistent auth state -> increased retries.
3) Rate limit enforcement is strictly per-key and not smoothing across short bursts; absence of token-level leaky-bucket smoothing leads to many 429s.
4) Misconfigured cache TTL in auth proxy (cache miss storm on token validation) - observed increased auth service calls during incidents.

Immediate mitigations tested / recommended:
- Short-term: increase client-side jitter on refresh (randomize within TTL window). I validated locally: adding +/- 5-15s jitter dramatically reduces simultaneous refreshes.
- Server-side: add a small per-key token grace window (e.g., accept previous token for 30s after rotation) to avoid immediate 401->retry storms. Discussed with auth-team.
- Rate limiting: consider introducing a brief request queue or burst window (token bucket with small burst allowance) instead of hard-cut 429 at bucket drain.
- Emergency: for affected keys, temporarily raise per-key limit or apply an account-level exemption for 1-2 minutes while we push SDK fix.

Commands/config changes tried (notes):
- Deployed auth-proxy change to log cache-miss rate (no behavior change) - observed spikes aligning with incidents.
- Simulated grace-window acceptance by modifying local auth mock (accept old tokens if within 30s) -> significantly fewer 429s in vegeta test.
- Raised per-key limit in staging to 4x for one key and replayed -> 401 still occurs but retries do not result in 429.

Open follow-ups / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm SDK versions in customer reports (v1.4.2 vs v1.3.x). Ask SDK team to ship jitter hotfix for refresh scheduling. (assign: Keisha)
- [ ] Implement server-side grace acceptance for rotated tokens (auth team to vet). (assign: Liam)
- [ ] Add telemetry for "token-refresh timestamp" per key to identify synchronized refresh windows. (assign: eng-infra)
- [ ] Consider back-pressure: if system observes many 401s from one key within short window, temporarily reduce allowed retry rate or return 429 with a Retry-After indicating jitter.
- [ ] Add a quick runbook entry to #sre-runbooks: steps to raise per-key quota for impacted customers and to alert SDK owners.

Notes to handoff:
- Slack snippets from customers: "we saw a bunch of 429s after our jobs rotated credentials at minute 00" (copy in linked artifacts).
- Attach vegeta results + staging auth logs when creating INF ticket.

Quick reproduction checklist (for whoever picks this up):
1) Use SDK v1.4.2 or force TTL expiry in mock client.
2) Launch 200 parallel clients that all schedule token refresh at same fixed offset (no jitter).
3) Watch for initial 401s then 429 flood; capture X-RateLimit-* headers and auth-service request counts.
4) Re-run with jitter +/-10s and verify spike disappears.

Last thoughts: this feels like a classic synchronized refresh -> retry amplification problem. Fix should be multi-pronged: immediate SDK jitter + short-term server-side grace + long-term smoothing/burst policy in rate limiter. Will draft a short RFC after infra/auth agree on grace approach.

-- Jordan
